attributes.probed_form:
MANDATORY STEP 1 FIRST (discipline 10b), BUILDLESS. MS v2's hypothesis asked whether savedBusy genuinely needs a callee-saved home across the whole function, or whether the target read gGameBusy nearer its single use. MEASURED with `fnasm ... 0x0:0x40` and `... 0x300:0x330` in both streams: the TARGET defines savedBusy at 0x34 (`lwz r27,gGameBusy`) and last-uses it at 0x310 (`stw r27,gGameBusy`); OURS defines at 0x34 (`lwz r30,gGameBusy`) and last-uses at 0x310 (`stw r30,gGameBusy`). Same two instruction indices, identical live range. MS v2's own cheapest_refuting_observation fires: the target did NOT read gGameBusy later, no live-range shortening is available, and the priority-by-live-range theory is refuted at zero build cost.

P1 (DISCARDED, NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL - object bytes unchanged). K&R old-style definition:
    void drawMemCardMessage(msg, options, count1, count2)
    const char* msg;
    char** options;
    s32 count1;
    s32 count2;
    {
MEASURED byte-identical. CATEGORICAL for the whole definition-FORM axis: MWCC canonicalises the K&R declarator list to the prototype form in the front end, so the construct never reaches the allocator's decision point and no respelling of it can. This also disposes of the prototype-presence variant, which is the same front-end fold and additionally could not be tried without changing the four call sites.

P2 (DISCARDED, REGRESSED real 126 -> 209, T204/O205, multiset 1t: ours-only -1 clrlwi at 0x17c). The MV width-class lever, used as a class-boundary READOUT rather than as a cure:
    u8 lineH;      /* was: int lineH; */
MEASURED - the cost: one added `clrlwi r30,r20,24`, so the retype is NOT free when the narrow value's producer is an int-returning call (`FontHeight(...) + 3`) rather than a truncating assignment; MV's freeness clause is bounded to the assignment case. THE READOUT, which is the point: lineH moved r27 -> r30 and blit moved r29 -> r28 - the narrow value rose WITHIN the local region exactly as MV predicts - while the four parameter copies at 0x14-0x20 stayed at r22/r23/r24/r25, unchanged to the register. Locals renumber; the parameter block does not.

P3 (DISCARDED, NEUTRAL-REARRANGED - object bytes CHANGED, real flat 126, wf_word_diff still exactly 61). Parameter-to-local conversion at entry:
    s32 sel = count2;      /* added as the last declaration */
    ...
    if (i == sel) {        /* was: if (i == count2) */
MEASURED: unlike P1 this edit DOES reach codegen (the object moved), which is what makes it a real probe of the partition rather than another fold. But the copy coalesced back onto count2's register, the parameter copies stayed at r22-r25, and the differing-word count did not move by one word.
attributes.residual:
BEST RETAINED: UNCHANGED at real 126, T204/O204, multiset 0t, 61 differing words. No source change kept.

WHAT THIS CORRECTS IN MS v2, all three points measured this run. (a) MS v2: 'the two unused registers are r23,r24 in the target and r27,r31 in ours'. FALSE - the target uses r23 at 0x124/0x144/0x14c/0x164/0x1c0/0x1e0/0x204/0x224/0x244/0x260/0x284/0x298/0x2bc/0x2d8 and r24 at 0x11c/0x158/0x26c/0x278/0x2a8/0x2cc/0x2e0; ours uses r27 and r31 at the mirror sites. BOTH streams use all TWELVE of r20-r31. (b) MS v2: 'the locals RELATIVE order is ALREADY IDENTICAL ... All 61 differing words are that one rotation'. FALSE - no register-level bijection exists at all. A max-weight assignment over every differing operand pair explains 83 of 109 callee-saved pairs (76.1%) and leaves 25 of 204 instructions unexplainable by ANY single bijection, because registers host several disjoint live ranges that the two builds partition differently: target r28 carries msg at 0x14/0x110/0x174/0x220 and then carries `addi r28,r1,72` (&lines) at 0x22c/0x254, while ours keeps msg in r22 throughout and puts &lines in r28. (c) Two of the 61 differing words are not callee-saved at all: 0x18c `addi r5,r3,60` (T) vs `addi r3,r3,60` (O) and 0x1b4 `srawi r0,r5,1` vs `srawi r0,r3,1`. ROOT CAUSE of the error, and the transferable lesson: MS v2's table was read from `fnasm ... 0x0:0xe0 --diff`, the first 0xe0 of a 0x330-byte body, and a prologue observation was generalised to the whole function.

WHAT SURVIVES MS v2 INTACT: the parameter block itself. Target msg/options/count1/count2 = r28/r29/r30/r31; ours = r22/r23/r24/r25. That is real, it is the largest single contributor to the 61 words, and it held through all three probes.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Buildless: `python tools/gdl/fnasm.py game/sys/memcard drawMemCardMessage 0x188:0x1b8 --diff` and check whether ANY instruction between 0x18c and 0x1b4 writes r3 or r5 in either stream. If both r3 and r5 are dead across the whole span in both builds, the choice is a free tiebreak with no source expression behind it, this hypothesis is refuted outright, and the function should be recorded source-exhausted.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: partly - the two differing volatile words ARE screened against target bytes and are the solid part (indices 99 and 109 of 204, quoted verbatim above). What is NOT screened is whether any source expression can reach that choice; no probe was spent on it this run because the parameter axis was the claimed scope.
hypothesis.statement: The only untried lever left is one that changes the LIVE RANGES rather than the numbering: eliminate or add a callee-saved value so the allocator packs differently. The concrete candidate is the boxH temporary at 0x18c-0x1b4, where the two builds already disagree on a VOLATILE register (target `addi r5,r3,60` / `srawi r0,r5,1` versus our `addi r3,r3,60` / `srawi r0,r3,1`) - the only two differing words in this function that are not callee-saved. Whatever decides that volatile choice is the same allocator state that decides the parameter partition, and it is the one difference with a plausible source expression (operand order or temporary structure in `boxH = (lineH + 6) * (count1 + TextMLines(msg)) + 60;`).
